title: halfshift-troubleshoot-docket-ishaan
content:
Half-shift notes (04:00-08:00 PDT) — rapid triage + followups

Shift context:
- Took half shift to cover Marcus's early morning. Goal: keep P99 latency under 500ms during peak job-run window (04:30-06:00).
- Quick checklist on wake: check PagerDuty, alerts dashboard (console -> per-route SLO), infra slack #sre-alerts.

Timeline / incidents handled:
1) 04:12 - Page: high-error-rate on hosted-api route /v1/generate (alert id A-4771)
   - First-action: rotated traffic to dedicated-fallback (policy: route -> dedicated-1) per standard fallback policy.
   - Symptoms: 5xx spikes concentrated on a single zone (us-west2-b). Errors were 502/504 from nginx-ingress sitting in front of serving runtime.
   - Quick triage: nginx logs showed repeated upstream connection resets to runtime pods on g4dn. Runtime logs showed OOM-kill events shortly before resets.
   - Mitigation: scaled serving-runtime-deployment replicas + applied emergency resource bump for pod template (cpu + mem) to give headroom. K8s horizontal autoscaler did not react in time (HPA metrics delay).
   - Outcome: error rate fell back to baseline ~04:36 after new pods warmed and cache primed.
   - Notes: likely sudden spike in seq-len for a small percentage of requests caused memory pressure + partial KV cache thrashing.
   - Followups: see TODOs below (RINF-1452 assigned).

2) 05:05 - Page: slow-embedding-worker queue (alert id A-4802)
   - Observed: worker pod latency for batch embeddings increased from 120ms -> 1.2s. Queue depth rose x6.
   - Action: cycled one worker replica to clear stuck batch; drained backlog with extra short-lived burst workers (manual k8s job).
   - Root cause hypothesis: a model quantization mis-config on the new variant caused single-batch slow path (PR 782 linked).
   - Outcome: queue drained by 05:22. Added temporary label to avoid routing to that variant.
   - Followups: add canary test for variant performance (RINF-1453).

Runbook gaps / quick notes observed during triage:
- Runbook: "runtime-memory-pressure" (v2) does not document KV cache sizing knobs or how cache eviction interacts with long-context requests. Put an explicit step for checking sequence-length distribution (logs) and workaround to enable conservative cache limits.
- Runbook: no clear play for autoscaler cold-start lag; need a step to fast-scale (kubectl patch HPA) rather than rely on HPA metric window.
- Logging: upstream nginx didn't include pod id in the initial error pages which slowed correlating 502s -> runtime pod restarts. Suggest adding pod metadata to access logs.

Immediate TODOs (short-term)
- [ ] RINF-1452: Write initial incident note + assign postmortem lead (assign to Anya). Due: 2027-09-20.
- [ ] RINF-1453: Create canary perf test for embedding variant; add to CI nightly. (Owner: Marco). Due: 2027-09-25.
- [ ] Add quick HPA emergency patch script to runbook and stash as runbook-snippets/k8s-fastscale.sh (me). Due: 2027-09-21.
- [ ] Add nginx access log pod-id injection (infra team). Ticket: infra#783. Due: 2027-09-26.

Longer-term (backlog)
- Revisit KV cache eviction policy: simulate long-context load (>8k tokens) and measure memory footprint / thrash. (Work with applied-ml).
- Evaluate model-variant deployment gating: perf smoke tests + rolling canaries with synthetic seq-length distribution.
- Consider adaptive autoscaler that uses request-rate + queue-depth rather than only CPU.

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Could add a short-running probe that sends synthetic long-context requests to a small % of pods to detect OOM slow-paths early. Might be a separate healthcheck type that checks memory allocation growth.
- For next handoff: short summary line in PD incident: "502 cascade due to runtime OOM under long-context workload; mitigated by replica scale + template bump; followups: runbook update, canary test, nginx logs."

Communications / Slack snippets for followup (copy-able):
- To #release: "Heads-up — we saw a transient 5xx spike on /v1/generate 04:12 PDT due to runtime memory pressure in us-west2-b. Traffic routed to dedicated fallback; error rate recovered by 04:36. Postmortem in RINF-1452 (Anya assigned)."
- To infra: "Please prioritize access-log pod-id injection (infra#783). Current debugging slowed significantly without pod IDs."

Open questions:
- Was there any upstream client sending long prefixes inadvertently? (ask product for recent customer jobs)
- Is the emergency resource bump safe for Dedicated customers who share node pools? Need billing/product sign-off if we use reserved capacity temporarily.

Attachments / links referenced:
- Jira RINF-1452 (incident)
- Jira RINF-1453 (canary tests)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/782
- Confluence stub: confluence://serving-runtime/postmortem-2027-09

Handoff summary for next oncall (short):
- Main risk: variant perf regressions + long-context memory thrash. Keep an eye on P99 latency and queue depth for embedding workers. If 5xx spike starts, rotate traffic to dedicated-fallback and scale serving-runtime replica set immediately (fastscale script).

End of shift quick checks performed:
- Confirmed PD incident routed to RINF-1452: yes
- Notified owners for followups: Anya, Marco
- Added runbook TODOs in local copy and created infra#783 stub

Personal notes: sleep at 08:30, ping Anya in morning to confirm postmortem cadence.
summary: Half-shift oncall log: handled a transient 5xx due to runtime OOM (scale + fallback), fixed embedding-worker slowdown by cycling worker and blocking bad variant; runbook gaps documented, followups created (RINF-1452, RINF-1453).
